turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Those waves out at Todos Santos already rolling two to three meters high, and the gusts pushing 30–50 kilometers an hour across the Pacific side.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: POSTA México just posted the National Weather Service notice, and small boats are staying in. [pause] It feels bigger than last week’s front.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yet right here in La Paz they just set the third community composter down in El Palmar II.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Diario Humano says it’s after the ones in Solidaridad and Los Mangos, and they’ll add two more parks next. Turns kitchen scraps into soil for the green spaces.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Cold front seven is due this week too. La Paz nights might touch seventeen degrees for the first time this season.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? The sea is testing the shore while we build these quiet piles of compost. [breath] Fishers warned about the old hotel at Punta Lobos long before the waves took part of it.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Debris from Hotel San Cristóbal sits under watch now so none reaches the water. [chuckle] One storm at a time.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And El Niño keeps lifting the tides at Puerto San Carlos. The researcher from UABCS says those extraordinary tides will stay with us through 2026.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The surf rises, the composter sits quietly turning. What keeps the balance?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. This is Radio BCS2050. Today we stay with Environment and chase one question.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does a single pile of compost teach us about the whole coast?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Pacific coast is facing 2 to 3 metre surf this week.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: POSTA México reports the National Weather Service notice covers Guerrero Negro through Todos Santos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And also Bahía Asunción, Puerto San Carlos, Puerto Adolfo López Mateos and El Pescadero.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Small boats already felt the last cold front when the Navy closed several ports.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Santa Rosalía, Loreto, San Carlos, Bahía Magdalena and López Mateos all shut down to small craft.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Now cold front number 7 is arriving.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It brings 30 to 50 km/h gusts over the Gulf too.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The front moves with an upper trough and the jet streams.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Cool air drops south across the whole peninsula.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That risk for small craft must feel familiar to fishers. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Palabra BCS says La Paz could drop to 17 degrees at night.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That would be the first time this season for the city.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The same front could bring lows of 16 to 17 degrees in the Santo Domingo valley.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What does that kind of shift feel like for people who work on the water?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The same front is expected to bring 5 to 25 millimetres of rain in the north.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Bahía Tortugas, Guerrero Negro and El Vizcaíno will see most of those showers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meanwhile La Paz is quietly building something else.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Diario Humano says the city just opened its third community composter in El Palmar II.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: After Solidaridad and Los Mangos, this one sits at the Centro Impulso.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Fundadores park in El Centenario and La Cima are next on the list.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 40 families already received home composters through the same programme.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What happens to the compost once it is ready?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It goes straight into the city’s green areas, with help from Semarnat and a fund from Chile.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: GeoCiclos brought the bin design from Chile.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Every scrap of kitchen waste becomes soil for the parks.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That feels like a small steady counter to the bigger weather swings.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Over in Todos Santos, another story is unfolding at the old Hotel San Cristóbal.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Nigua reports Profepa inspected after a wall collapsed on 11 November.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Tres Santos project had reported the collapse and started demolishing damaged sections.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: No wastewater or chemicals reached the sea, and no wildlife was harmed.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They are still reviewing the environmental permit and how the demolition waste is handled.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Profepa will check whether demolition stays inside the original permit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Any loose debris has to stay away from the dunes at Punta Lobos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Profepa may launch a formal inspection if anything looks off.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The site sits right at Punta Lobos, so any mistake could reach the water quickly.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: How do you weigh one community composter against the risk at that hotel? [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Both stories are about the same coastline trying to stay ahead of what the next front brings.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Ciudad Constitución sits inland in Comondú, an agri hub with room for desal pilots and irrigation works.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Pacific coast nearby still feels the desert wind every morning.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mulegé north stretches sparse through Vizcaíno, where the CFE Oasis H2 project was announced in September 2026.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Guerrero Negro and Bahía Asunción lie right there on that same corridor.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: POSTA México reported the National Weather Service notice 638 calling for two to three meter surf along those western shores.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 30–50 km/h gusts too. Small boats stay tied up.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The notice names Puerto Adolfo López Mateos and Todos Santos among the spots feeling that swell.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: In early November the Navy closed Santa Rosalía, Loreto and Bahía Magdalena to small craft during cold front four.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep wondering how a fisher in Puerto San Carlos reads that forecast before dawn. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The same wind that helps the H2 experiments also pushes the swell.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you ask the workers running the desal pilots in Comondú?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: How they keep the aquifer from dropping when every extra liter goes to the fields.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The constraint list names irrigation stress and energy for pumping.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet the place still holds land for productive investment beyond tourism.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: In Vizcaíno the isolation gives space for remote energy trials.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: But water and labor remain thin on the ground.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What draws a family to keep working that thin soil year after year?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The light at dusk across the flats, maybe, and the quiet that follows the wind.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meanwhile La Paz just set its third community composter in El Palmar II.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: After the ones in Solidaridad and Los Mangos, and they handed out 40 home composters to families already.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The programme runs with Semarnat and a group from Chile turning organic waste into soil for green areas.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It runs through the Pacific Alliance Cooperation Fund and GeoCiclos at Centro Impulso.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Fundadores park in El Centenario and La Cima are next on the list.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A road out there feels more like a question than a line on the map. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. What does the desert teach the people who stay?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I would ask them that, quietly, on a calm evening after the surf warning passes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And listen while the light changes over the salt flats.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Luz, when I line up these last few weeks, the same line keeps appearing under every story.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The coast itself, and what we keep asking it to carry.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. Meganoticias reports El Niño lifted waves 15–30 cm at Puerto San Carlos and let the sea through the old barriers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And the same swell took the ground out from under the hotel at Punta Lobos. Fishers had been saying since 2015 that the development changed the beach.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. Tribuna de México adds that tides could hit 2.12–2.55 m in Bahía Magdalena later this month.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That extra reach changes everything for the low streets in San Carlos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Gringo Gazette notes Semarnat still gave conditional approval for another 30.96 ha at Camarón Beach, even while it listed the impacts.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the thread is not just the tides. It is every new foundation placed where the next high water will test it.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal’s earlier Foresight already named this: coastal erosion joining the 2050 ceiling, right after Polo and Rachel.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And the new bill would let municipalities help set the reserves. That feels like someone finally looking at the local end of the same thread.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yet the artificial reefs in La Paz Bay are also part of it. Meganoticias says they are a direct answer to warming water and lost habitat.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So one project tries to rebuild what another project and the changed sea are taking away.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The surprise for me is how quiet the infrastructure question stays. [pause] The tyres that washed out of the arroyos after one rain, the missing quantitative load numbers in the East Cape pack, the gaps the knowledge graph keeps flagging.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias counted over 350 tyres pulled from El Médano after the last rain.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Ha, of course. One storm and the hidden dumps become the next cleanup bill.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: No one has drawn the single map that shows where the next wall or the next reef actually meets the next storm tide.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Foro Mar de Cortés keeps talking about doubling the regional economy while the same waters delay the whale-shark season.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It is the same tension the portal recorded last month: growth ambition against the limits already visible on the shore.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the desert teach a city when the sea keeps arriving farther inland?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That every pipe, every lot line, every unlined arroyo is already part of the coastal system.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the thread runs through all of them, whether the next approval notices it or not.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Did you know one protected stretch here covers 2,546,790.25 hectares?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mostly inside Mulegé.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That is 77% of the whole municipality.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The next protected zone covers 112,437.07 hectares and stays all on land.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Really? So the map covers almost the entire drive.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So when you drive the long road south from Loreto, almost everything you pass is inside that boundary.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That same boundary keeps the rock paintings in the Sierra de San Francisco safe from the next storm surge.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And it protects the whale lagoons that UNESCO recognized back in 1993 as part of our shared heritage.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert itself becomes the quiet partner in every plan.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The dunes and the sea share the same rules now that the tide reaches the streets of El Centenario.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Polo showed how fast that shared line can break when the levee failed at Puerto San Carlos last month.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What happens to a fishing village when the sea and the dunes both count as the same protected body?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The rules travel with the tide and with the dust.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep picturing the water people carry home each day.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That water starts inside the protected recharge zones farther south.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The same map that keeps the whales also keeps the wells.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: UNESCO called the place a refuge back in 1993.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A refuge that now has to hold both the old rock paintings and the new desal plant.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The desert teaches the city to ask first before it builds.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Forum at Los Cabos discussed how growth must respect those same protected recharge zones across the state.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They talked about tripling investment while keeping the whole Gulf under one single regional plan for 2050.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. [pause] And the sea answers back with every swell.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: When the high tide on 25 October pushed into the streets of El Centenario and El Conchalito, those dunes were the first thing that slowed the water.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 15 to 30 centimeters more wave height at Puerto San Carlos changes the edge of every refuge.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [chuckle] The same line on the map now has to hold both the old paintings and the next big swell.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would the fishers in Puerto San Carlos ask the planners first?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They would point to the levee that Polo already breached last month.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What if the real map of this place is not the one we drive, but the one written in quiet documents.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The ones that decide whether a project even gets considered.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. POERBCS sits there with its 56 UGAs and three named policies.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Aprovechamiento Sustentable, Preservación, Protección.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Those words decide what can happen along the coast or in the desert.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [pause] And yet most people never open the page.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep wondering what the desert would say if it could read those lines first.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It would ask whether the light still reaches the water.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the hidden design is really a set of questions asked before anything is built.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The ontology lists them plainly. Viability first.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Water from the DMA and the aquifers, energy through SIBCS and CFE.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Then the protected areas and the coastal pressure.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: For East Cape the graph shows aquifer 0318 next to Cabo Pulmo ANP.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [chuckle] One line on paper, and the whole settlement pressure changes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Loreto carries the 2014 POEL and the federal WWTP inventory.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mulegé still watches the Transpeninsular highway and the desert spine.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The library books from 1993 and 2010 keep asking how density and street design quietly shape how far we have to travel for water or work.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Peter Calthorpe's book on compact regions feels like it was written for the long road south.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the 2013 guide on street retrofits shows how a single curb can cool an entire block.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the everyday object is not the pipe or the road.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It is the page that decides whether either one can exist.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [pause] And whether the next page will still have room for the sea and the light.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I wonder how those older studies on travel demand would read the gaps we still carry today.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Especially when the knowledge graph marks quantitative load as incomplete for East Cape.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That leaves the sea and the dunes holding the real question mark.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. One quiet document at a time.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal’s vision for the coast by 2050 starts with what is already visible on the shoreline.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Surge, erosion and flooding keep pressing against what was built too close to the water.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: El Niño is already lifting wave heights in Puerto San Carlos by 15–30 cm, according to UABCS.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That single measurement makes the risk feel closer than any long-range map. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The aspiration is a coast that stays habitable by restoring barriers and stepping back from the risk zones first.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Retreat and restoration before any new line of hotels or homes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The levers are clear on paper. Finish the environmental reviews already open, like the one at Hotel San Cristóbal in Punta Lobos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the debris and the precedent do not simply wash away with the next surge.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And keep relocation at the front of every decision rather than an afterthought.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Respect the ANP and coastal-planning ceilings in East Cape, Loreto and the Pacific corridor before scaling anything new.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The tendencia that still holds is not one coastal formula repeated from south to north.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It is a polycentric system where each place keeps its own role.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos under water and power stress, East Cape in tension with protected areas, Todos Santos and El Pescadero as the Pacific amenity spine.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Paz as the service and water-energy node, Loreto as tourism-conservation anchor, Comondú with more room for agriculture.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Northern Mulegé remains thinly documented, now with a remote generation tender.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The conditions for that system to work are straightforward.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: New growth only where water and energy show real margin, without pretending NOM-011 credit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And Comondú and the north add production without emptying services or ANPs.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: On the watchlist right now is Punta Lobos and the Hotel San Cristóbal case.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The technical finding on causes and the Profepa review of the authorisation and debris handling.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That review may tell us whether the levers actually move when the next wave arrives.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. [pause] The portal notes coast and climate accounts for just 2 items this week, with the EWMA at 5.55 and direction flat.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Without a modelled 2050 shoreline the aspiration stays simple: keep the coast regenerative by letting each vocation hold its own place under the light.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep coming back to this feeling that the coast is asking something of us. What does it want us to understand about living here?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Not to push forward, but to make room. [chuckle] It is funny how that simple shift changes everything we think we need to do.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Room for the sand to move, for the mangroves to hold. I wonder what that looks like on a daily basis for people who have lived by the water their whole lives.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And for us to listen before we build again. Have you noticed how the waves keep reminding us of that?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What if the next thing we do is simply step aside? [pause] Just let things breathe where they need to.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [breath] Let the edge stay wild a little longer. That might be the hardest part, waiting without acting right away.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That quiet choice feels like the real work. It connects us back to the place in a different way, almost like an old agreement we are renewing.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. It is less about control and more about partnership with the sea and the desert meeting here. What would that partnership look like for you?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A daily practice of noticing before deciding. That sense of partnership could guide us forward.
